project.commit_note: The exact staged vulnerable checkout reviewed here is `b70a1738468cc64b4952f2f3bc98ba6db4edfd22`; its line map matches the saved ASan frames `ddsi_type_unref_impl_locked:1060`, `ddsi_xt_type_fini:1617`, `ddsi_type_new:429`, and the allocation context `ddsi_xt_type_init_impl:1379`. The staged patch `1ae6bb9985c05f8742cb31c0bd46f3c7bd8777bd` adds `xt->_u.map.c.element_type = NULL;` in the plain-map key-dependency error path and makes `ddsi_type_unref_locked()` NULL-safe, which matches the reviewed stale-pointer cleanup bug.

bug_description.normalized: A malformed XTypes TypeMapping can make `ddsi_xt_type_init_impl()` take the `DDS_XTypes_TI_PLAIN_MAP_SMALL` path, register and store a map-element dependency, then fail while registering the map key dependency and manually unref that child without clearing `xt->_u.map.c.element_type`. `ddsi_type_new()` then finalizes the half-built parent type, `ddsi_xt_type_fini()` unreferences the stale element pointer a second time, and `ddsi_type_unref_impl_locked()` reads the freed child type's refcount, triggering the reported heap-use-after-free read.

source.description: First project parser statement that consumes the attacker-controlled blob and materializes the `DDS_XTypes_TypeMapping` object whose complete-identifier array later supplies the forged map type identifier.
source.value_from: The staged witness is exactly the 854-byte file `gt_results/arvo_56837/poc` (sha256 `32d5410a27b47b11476ffcf64621ba52ace1591e49ffa0b5559c3ec8476168ec`). The saved run proves `ddsi_typemap_deser()` accepts it as an XCDR2 `DDS_XTypes_TypeMapping`, because execution reaches `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput` line 88 and then crashes in `ddsi_type_unref_impl_locked()`.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer sink. The second unref reaches this decrement through a stale `struct ddsi_type *` pointer, so reading `type->refc` consumes four bytes from already-freed heap memory.
sink.note: The saved ASan trace reports `heap-use-after-free READ of size 4` at `/src/cyclonedds/src/core/ddsi/src/ddsi_typelib.c:1060:7` on address `0x615000001178`, 504 bytes into the freed 512-byte region `[0x615000000f80, 0x615000001180)`.

root_cause.description: Root cause. On the plain-map key-dependency error path, the code manually unreferences `xt->_u.map.c.element_type` but leaves that field pointing at the freed child before returning error, so later parent cleanup reuses the dangling pointer.
root_cause.note: The saved allocation stack resolves the first dependency registration to `ddsi_xt_type_init_impl:1379`, proving the `DDS_XTypes_TI_PLAIN_MAP_SMALL` branch executed. The staged fix adds `xt->_u.map.c.element_type = NULL;` here and makes `ddsi_type_unref_locked()` return early on `NULL`, so `ddsi_xt_type_fini()` no longer re-unrefs the already-released child.

parser_admitted.description: The staged 854-byte blob passes `dds_stream_normalize_data()` as a valid enough XCDR2 `DDS_XTypes_TypeMapping` payload. Otherwise `ddsi_typemap_deser()` would return `NULL` at lines 222-226 and the saved run could not reach `ddsi_type_ref_proxy()` or the later ASan crash.

tainted_value_origin.description: The concrete tainted value carried into the vulnerable project path is the selected complete type identifier copied out of the deserialized typemap. On the witnessed run that identifier drives the `DDS_XTypes_TI_PLAIN_MAP_SMALL` branch later confirmed by the allocation stack at `ddsi_xt_type_init_impl:1379`.

fine_trace.note: Source. `dds_stream_read` materializes attacker-controlled `identifier_object_pair_complete` and `identifier_complete_minimal` arrays inside `typemap`. The saved run proves this succeeds for the exact 854-byte witness because execution reaches `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput` line 88 and then the project-code UAF sink.

For one parsed typemap entry, the harness finds a matching minimal identifier and the non-NONE guard passes. It copies the attacker-controlled complete identifier into `type_info` and hands that exact value to `ddsi_type_ref_proxy()` as a COMPLETE type id.

Project code now selects the attacker-copied COMPLETE identifier from `type_info` and, because `gv->typelib` has no existing entry for it, sends that identifier into `ddsi_type_new()`. This is the first project-side use of the specific type id chosen in step 2.

`ddsi_type_new()` allocates a fresh parent `struct ddsi_type` with zeroed fields and passes its `xt` subobject to `ddsi_xt_type_init_impl()` for population from the attacker-controlled complete identifier.

The saved allocation stack records the nested child allocation at `ddsi_xt_type_init_impl:1379`, proving the selected complete type identifier is `DDS_XTypes_TI_PLAIN_MAP_SMALL`. This branch marks the parent `xt` as a map and stores the successfully resolved element dependency in `xt->_u.map.c.element_type`.

Root cause. The second dependency registration on the attacker-controlled map `key_identifier` fails, so the error path manually unreferences the element child from step 5. It does not clear `xt->_u.map.c.element_type` before returning error, leaving the parent map state with a dangling child pointer. The fix inserts `xt->_u.map.c.element_type = NULL;` here.

The manual unref from step 6 drops the child dependency's last reference, so `ddsi_type_fini()` frees that child `struct ddsi_type`. AddressSanitizer's free stack names this exact line as the freeing context for the later UAF address.

Because step 6 returned an error, `ddsi_type_new()` immediately finalizes the half-built parent type instead of inserting it into `gv->typelib`. That cleanup reuses whatever state remains in `(*type)->xt`.

Parent cleanup sees the stale `xt` as a map and sends `xt->_u.map.c.element_type` through `ddsi_type_unref_locked()` again. Because step 6 left that field pointing at the child freed in step 7, this is the second unref of the same object.

ASan sink. The second unref from step 9 passes the freed child pointer as `type`, and evaluating `--type->refc` reads four bytes from the freed 512-byte `struct ddsi_type` allocation. The saved crash reports this exact read at line 1060.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_free_context: The ASan free stack shows the first free originates from the small-map key-dependency error path inside `ddsi_xt_type_init_impl`, then reaches `ddsi_type_fini:382`. The staged patch repairs that exact path by nulling `xt->_u.map.c.element_type` immediately after the manual unref.
cross_validation.trace_consistent_with_stack: The saved crash stack matches the trace tail `ddsi_type_new -> ddsi_type_fini -> ddsi_xt_type_fini -> ddsi_type_unref_locked -> ddsi_type_unref_impl_locked`; the saved free stack matches the first-free path `ddsi_xt_type_init_impl -> ddsi_type_unref_locked -> ddsi_type_unref_impl_locked -> ddsi_type_fini`; and the saved allocation stack resolves the child allocation to `ddsi_xt_type_init_impl:1379`, proving the `DDS_XTypes_TI_PLAIN_MAP_SMALL` branch used in steps 5-6.
cross_validation.tainted_value_reaches_sink: Closed. The deserialized typemap supplies the complete type identifier copied into `type_info` at step 2; project code carries that identifier into the `PLAIN_MAP_SMALL` initializer at step 5, stores the child pointer in `xt->_u.map.c.element_type`, frees that same child at step 7, and then reuses the stale field at steps 9-10.

poc.trigger: Stage 01's saved vulnerable run executed `PYTHONPATH=gt_generation python3 -m gt_toolkit arvo-workspace --result-dir /mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_56837 run --version vulnerable --expect crash`, which fed the staged `poc` file to `fuzz_type_object` and reproduced `AddressSanitizer: heap-use-after-free READ of size 4` with crash stack `ddsi_type_unref_impl_locked -> ddsi_type_unref_locked -> ddsi_xt_type_fini`.

format.name: raw DDS XTypes TypeMapping blob
format.contract: Exactly the 854-byte blob stored at `gt_results/arvo_56837/poc` (sha256 `32d5410a27b47b11476ffcf64621ba52ace1591e49ffa0b5559c3ec8476168ec`). On the witnessed run, `ddsi_typemap_deser()` accepts it as a `DDS_XTypes_TypeMapping`, the harness finds a non-NONE complete/minimal identifier pair and copies the complete identifier into `type_info`, and the saved allocation stack proves that selected complete identifier takes the `DDS_XTypes_TI_PLAIN_MAP_SMALL` branch in `ddsi_xt_type_init_impl` at line 1379. The same map identifier must register its `element_identifier` successfully and then fail while registering `key_identifier`, so the error path frees `xt->_u.map.c.element_type` before parent cleanup rereads that stale pointer. The trigger semantics recorded here do not generalize beyond this exact staged blob.
